newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain seeks talks with Qatar to end border row.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain seeks talks with Qatar to end border row.

text.p: Bahrain's Crown Prince Sheikh Hamad bin Isa al-Khalifa in remarks published on Saturday called for a summit with Qatar to end a territorial dispute.

"We have called for a summit to settle disputes between Bahrain and Qatar and we still call for (the summit) because our final goal was to call for unity between us and our brothers in Qatar," Sheikh Hamad told Bahraini newspapers.
"This is not impossible if true intentions persist," said Sheikh Hamad, also Commander-in-Chief of Bahrain's armed forces.

"Both countries have been one state in recent history. The unity will achieve historic, geographic, political and economic integration. The unity...is needed and is in accordance with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) treaty."
Bahrain and Qatar are members of the Gulf Cooperation Council, an economic, political and military alliance that also groups Saudi Arabia, Oman, United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.
Doha and Manama are locked in a dispute over a number of barren but potentially oil and gas-rich islands, sand banks and reefs controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.
Sheikh Hamad renewed a call to Qatar to withdraw the case it had taken to the International Court of Justice in the Hague to settle the dispute, urging it to accept Saudi arbitration.
Qatar, which unilaterally applied to the world court in 1991, says it will only withdraw the case if Saudi mediation is successful.
Bahrain has refused to accept the jurisdiction of the court, which decided in January that it had jurisdiction and is expected to produce a verdict by the end of 1996.
Sheikh Hamad confirmed that Bahrain would boycott a summit of Gulf Arab leaders due to be held in Doha in December if Qatar did not withdraw the case form the court.
